gaps.sentence: I ___ the dentist on Thursday afternoon — I booked it last week.
gaps.explanation: A personal arrangement already made takes the present continuous: am seeing.

gaps.sentence: She has bought the paint, so tomorrow she ___ the kitchen.
gaps.hint: an intention already decided before speaking
gaps.explanation: An intention decided before the moment of speaking uses 'be going to': is going to paint.

gaps.sentence: She ___ to the gym three times a week, mostly before work.
gaps.hint: three times a week shows a routine
gaps.explanation: Frequency expressions like 'three times a week' describe habits, which take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: By the time you read this letter, I ___ the country.
gaps.explanation: An action completed before a future point takes the future perfect: will have left.

gaps.sentence: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
gaps.hint: a timeless scientific fact takes present simple
gaps.explanation: General truths and scientific facts take the present simple: boils.

gaps.sentence: The taxi ___ as soon as you come out of the terminal — look for a blue shirt.
gaps.hint: in progress at the future arrival moment
gaps.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous: will be waiting.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the car tonight, so take a taxi into town.
gaps.hint: a future activity in progress as reason
gaps.explanation: The future continuous can express something in progress around a future time, here as a polite reason: will be using.
